name: Sky Records
editorial_article: Sky Records was a pivotal independent German record label founded in 1975 by Günter Körber in Hamburg, acting as a crucial sanctuary for the evolving sounds of Krautrock, Kosmische Musik, and progressive electronic experimentation. Emerging from the legacy of Brain Records, where Körber had previously worked, Sky Records provided a creative home for influential artists who were pushing the boundaries of synthesis, ambience, and avant-garde composition. Its establishment helped maintain the continuity of the experimental German scene during a period of transition in the late 1970s.\n\nThe label's cultural significance was bolstered by its signing of Cluster, whose collaborative work with Brian Eno—most notably the 1977 album 'Cluster & Eno'—became a cornerstone of the label’s catalog and critical reputation. Throughout its existence, Sky Records served as a catalyst for both the pioneers of early electronic music and a new wave of ambient and experimental performers, including Michael Rother, Asmus Tietchens, and Conrad Schnitzler. Its output ranged from dense, motorik-inflected progressive rock to ethereal synthesizer soundscapes. Although the label ceased new releases in 1998 and was formally dissolved in 1997, its catalog remains a essential reference point for the evolution of European electronic music, with much of its output later preserved and celebrated through reissues by labels like Bureau B. By bridging the gap between early 70s avant-garde and the ambient developments of the 80s, Sky Records cemented its legacy as one of the most important imprints in the history of German experimental music. Its dissolution marked the end of an era for the independent Hamburg label circuit, but its influence continues to resonate in contemporary electronic and experimental spheres.
editorial_description: Sky Records was a pivotal independent German record label founded in 1975 by Günter Körber in Hamburg, acting as a sanctuary for Krautrock and electronic experimentation.
